paragraphs.dominant_move: five aspects -> secondary metrics -> playoff-data example
AHP weights -> FSE memberships -> entropy weights -> grades
media offsets -> component hit scores -> AM -> basketball top five
six time periods -> gender rerun -> football and hockey transfer
strengths and weaknesses -> nontechnical explanation -> future work
Sports Illustrated audience -> century-wide multi-sport coach decision
task 1 -> articulate metrics and build a model
task 2 -> construct a model-performance evaluation system
task 3 -> consider time, gender, and sport transfer
task 4 -> analyze parameters and wider applicability
prior media lists -> existing ranking context
Sections 2-9 -> definitions, metrics, models, extensions, discussion, communication, future work

global_organization_chain: The six-paragraph summary moves from five aspects and secondary metrics through AHP, FSE, external hit scores, aggregation, extensions, sensitivity, and final communication.
The introduction identifies the Sports Illustrated decision, four required tasks, two prior method families, and a section-by-section route to the deliverables.
The notation binds annual records, AHP quantities, fuzzy and entropy quantities, aggregation weights, and assumptions about omitted factors, data accuracy, and media rankings.
The metric chapter expands five aspects into eighteen secondary indicators and defines wins, losses, SRS, SOS, playoff classes, honors, and contribution scores.
The data section fixes a 75-coach basketball roster, shows coach and season tables, and interpolates missing SRS and SOS from rankings generated by other metrics.
The AHP section builds a three-level hierarchy, pairwise matrix, eigenvector weights, consistency checks, a weighted grade, and a top-ten ranking.
The first FSE stage converts the five aspect definitions into explicit coach-grade formulas for records, game quality, playoffs, honors, and contribution.
The second FSE stage normalizes aspect grades into memberships and derives characteristic shares, entropy, diversity, criterion weights, and a final grade.
The evaluation section compares AHP and FSE with media-ranking offset distances and a hit score while exposing the benchmark dependence.
The aggregation section weights AHP and FSE inversely by their offset distances and reports the combined rank and hit scores.
The gender extension reruns the model on a women-basketball roster and compares its top ten with a Yahoo list.
The time extension divides NCAA history into six periods, assigns judgmental time weights, rebuilds annual metrics, and compares three changed rankings and hit scores.
The cross-sport extension maps basketball playoff and honor fields to football and ice hockey, adjusts metrics and rules, applies time weights, and reports new lists.
The first sensitivity study compares three membership-function families, traces entropy-weight changes over k, and chooses a hit-score maximizing configuration.
The second sensitivity study varies the win-to-loss weight ratio and selects the ratio two using the same media hit-score benchmark.
The third sensitivity study varies the AHP share, tracks rank changes, and selects an AHP weight near 0.1 to 0.2 by hit score.
The exploration remaps five evaluation aspects to 43 U.S. presidents and reports a top-ten list as a transfer demonstration.
The closing assessment preserves the model's breadth, explicit metrics, and adjustment workflow before stating data, subjectivity, and reproducibility limits.
The final ranked table and nontechnical explanation translate the model route into lists and a sports-fan-facing account of scores and relative position.
The future-work paragraph asks for broader data and improved quantification, while the references identify sources without freezing the data or code.
The final warning pass records table, symbol, coefficient, benchmark, generalization, and reproducibility defects without replacing positive learning.

main_argument_chains.claim: A coach-ranking decision becomes inspectable when five aspects and eighteen secondary indicators feed two explicitly different component models.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use component grades only with the declared roster, definitions, sources, and weighting contracts.

main_argument_chains.claim: Model aggregation is traceable when external offsets, hit scores, component grades, and aggregation weights remain distinct.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat AM as optimized fit to selected media lists, not independent ranking truth.

main_argument_chains.claim: Gender, era, sport, and president applications require declared input remapping and their own validation rather than inherited validity.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Report each extension as a scoped demonstration until held-out receiving-domain evidence exists.

main_argument_chains.claim: Sensitivity plots are most useful when the varied function, parameter, score response, rank response, and benchmark dependence are all visible.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Separate parameter selection from final evaluation and report uncertainty around rank changes.

main_argument_chains.claim: The final lists retain analytical value when the nontechnical explanation reconnects them to aspects, scores, and rank meaning.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Publish the audience artifact with source, benchmark, transfer, and reproducibility disclosures.

The three-level hierarchy maps the evaluation goal to five criteria and their alternatives.
The displayed matrix, CW vector, CI, CR, and secondary vectors make the intended AHP calculation inspectable.
The AHP top-ten table binds coach names, grades, and rank order.
The matrix layout shows coaches by five normalized aspect memberships before entropy weighting.
The FSE result table joins five aspect values, entropy quantities, weights, grades, a duplicate X3 header, and the truncated Mike Krzy label.
The component-evaluation table compares top-five, lower-five, and total distances and hit scores for AHP and FSE.
The aligned AHP, FSE, and AM orders show how aggregation changes the top ten.
The model-comparison table presents component and aggregate top-five and top-ten hit scores.
The women-basketball table exposes the subgroup records used by the gender application.

The before-and-after AHP columns expose grade and rank movement under period weights.
The before-and-after FSE columns expose grade, rank, and hit-score changes.

Basketball playoff and honor fields are aligned with football bowls and ice-hockey stages before transfer.

Sport-specific top lists make the transferred outputs scannable.

Aggregation-weight plots jointly expose rank trajectories and hit score as the AHP share changes.
